title: Coaching Staff
description: Preserves coaching changes, historical tendencies, role philosophy and uncertainty about attribution across head coaches and coordinators.
principles: Distinguish head coach, coordinator and complete staff responsibilities.
Historical tendencies are evidence, not automatic guarantees in a new roster context.
Preserve independently reusable staff takes when multiple players or positions are affected.
Keep uncertainty about play-calling and attribution explicit.

dimensions.description: Who joined, left or changed responsibility.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve role and timing of each material staff change.
detection_questions: Who is expected to call plays?

dimensions.description: Prior pace, pass rate, personnel or positional usage.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Retain the tendency and the context in which it occurred.
detection_questions: What historical evidence does the source use?
Was it stable across teams or personnel?

dimensions.description: How the staff deploys positions, committees and specialists.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Explain the role mechanism and affected positions.
detection_questions: Does the staff concentrate work or rotate?

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve grouping implications for snaps and target availability.
detection_questions: Which personnel packages materially affect fantasy roles?

dimensions.description: Tempo, pass/run balance and situational decisions.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Keep source-supported tendencies and uncertainty around play-calling control.
detection_questions: Who controls pace and play selection?

dimensions.description: Rookie usage, veteran preference and developmental history.
dimensions.preservation_expectation: Preserve the evidence and avoid treating small samples as rules.
detection_questions: Does the staff trust rookies or specialists?
How does the source support that?

dimensions.description: Installation time, continuity and change risk.

dimensions.preservation_expectation: Link affected entities while keeping the coach/staff thesis independent.
detection_questions: Who is directly affected and through what mechanism?

dimensions.description: Uncertainty over whether outcomes came from coach, coordinator, roster or game state.
detection_questions: Can the source safely attribute the tendency?

passing: Preserve the reference only where it is needed to understand another argument.
Do not create an artificial standalone evaluation.
brief: Preserve the conclusion and its immediate qualifier or condition.
Do not expand beyond what the source supports.
substantive: Preserve the conclusion plus the meaningful reason, condition, risk or uncertainty supplied by the source.
Keep format, price or time-horizon distinctions when they materially change the view.
deep: Preserve the complete major reasoning chain rather than only the final verdict.
Represent every materially discussed dimension, including competing positive and negative cases.
Keep disagreements, uncertainty, conditions and failure paths.
structural: Preserve the broad thesis, its mechanism, its scope and the subjects it affects.
Create independently reusable context takes rather than burying the thesis inside one player.

review_questions: Are coaching responsibilities and play-calling ownership accurately distinguished?
Are historical tendencies presented with context and limitations?
Can the staff take be reused for multiple affected players?
Are scheme and coaching claims separated when they are not identical?
forbidden_distortions: Do not attribute every historical team outcome to one coach.
Do not treat a new staff as guaranteed to repeat old usage.
Do not collapse head coach, coordinator and play caller into one identity.
Do not produce player recommendations during source extraction.
extension_signals: A recurring coaching role or responsibility is missing.
The source introduces a new method for attributing play-calling or development.
A new staff-level relation to players or units is needed.
The profile cannot represent committee or personnel-use nuance.
